 Dated this the 08th day of November, 2024
 Order

An order dismissing a petition seeking discharge under Section 227 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, is under challenge in this revision petition filed under Section 397 read with Section 401 of the Code.
The petitioner is the sole accused in S.C. No.491 of 2018, now pending trial before the additional Sessions Judge-II (Special), Kottayam.
2. The offences alleged are punishable under Sections 376(2)(f)(k)(n) and Section 506(i) of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.

3. The learned Additional Sessions Judge held that the plea of the petitioner for discharge is essentially based on the documents he has produced, and as documents produced by the accused are not liable to be looked into for deciding whether or not a charge is framed, the petition could not be entertained.
The petitioner assails the said findings.
Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Public Prosecutor.
5. The petitioner has been conducting a Nursing College at Kuruppanthara.
The victim was a student there.
They went together to Dharghamani Hospital, Maharashtra, in connection with arranging nursing practice to the victim.

In the course of travel in and later at the office of the nursing school,
the petitioner was said to have been subjected to sexual intercourse.
Stating that the victim was subjected to such sexual acts without her informed consent, the prosecution was launched.
6. The case of the petitioner is that the very allegations levelled against him are false.

He places reliance on train tickets and hospital records in order to substantiate his contention that he was not available at the place of occurrence on the alleged dates of the incident i.e., on 30.06.2016 and 05.05.2017.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the petitioner would submit that the trial ought to have considered the improbability in the version of the defacto complainant and when there is no such 2024:KER:83491 consideration in the impugned order, it is liable to be reversed.
As stated, the main offence alleged is rape.
When the victim states that she was subjected to sexual acts and such acts were without her consent, it is not possible to have a finding that that version cannot form the basis for framing a charge.
The inconsistencies pointed out in the oral assertions of the victim are matters requiring considered only during trial.
Impact of such contradictions is concerning the credibility of the victim which is a post charge exercise.
Therefore, the contention of the petitioner that on account of the inconsistencies that appeared on the materials on record, a discharge should be recorded cannot be countenanced.

8. The court below placed reliance on the law laid down by the Apex Court in State of Orissa v.
Debendra Nath Padhi [2005 (1) SCC 568] to repel the contention of the petitioner that the documents he has produced should be looked into for deciding correctness of the prosecution allegations.

entities.text:
State of Orissa v.
Debendra Nath Padhi [2005 (1) SCC 568]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I find no infirmity in that view.

As held in the said decision going by the provisions of Section 227 of the Code, the materials 2024:KER:83491 produced by the prosecution alone can be considered in order to decide whether a grave suspicion warranting framing of a charge is made out or not.
Therefore, the documents produced by the petitioner before the trial court, purpose of which is to support his plea of alibi, cannot be looked into at this stage.

In the said circumstances,
challenge to the impugned order can only fail.
Accordingly, this revision petition is dismissed.
